Simplified Portuguese administrative boundaries

Source: R/data.R
boundaries.Rd

Pre-simplified sf objects derived from CAOP (Carta Administrativa Oficial de Portugal). All levels are topologically consistent: higher-level boundaries are dissolved from simplified freguesias, guaranteeing aligned edges. Each level carries its own identity columns (official codes and names) plus aggregated area_ha, so every dataset joins directly against user data or against pt_registry.

Usage

pt_freguesias

pt_municipios

pt_distritos

pt_nuts1

pt_nuts2

pt_nuts3

pt_uls

pt_reg_saude

pt_aces

pt_uls_municipio

pt_aces_municipio

Format

An sf data frame with MULTIPOLYGON geometry.

Source

Direção-Geral do Território (DGT), CAOP. https://www.dgterritorio.gov.pt/cartografia/cartografia-tematica/caop

Details

Common columns (present where applicable to the level):

dtmnfr

6-digit freguesia code (distrito + municipio + freguesia), zero-padded character. Freguesias only.

dtmn

4-digit municipality code (first 4 digits of dtmnfr).

dt

2-digit distrito/ilha code.

nuts1_cod, nuts2_cod, nuts3_cod

NUTS 2024 codes in full Eurostat form (PT1, PT19, PT191, ...).

freguesia, municipio, distrito_ilha, nuts1, nuts2, nuts3

Official names.

designacao_simplificada

The freguesia's name without the "União das freguesias de" prefix. Freguesias only.

perimetro_km

Perimeter in kilometres, as CAOP gives it. Freguesias only.

area_ha

Area in hectares, summed from the constituent freguesias.

n_freguesias, n_municipios

Number of constituent units.

Geometries use WGS84 (EPSG:4326) and cover all of Portugal (Continente, Açores, and Madeira).

A multi-layer GeoPackage containing the same data is also bundled at inst/extdata/caop_simplified.gpkg, with one layer per level:

gpkg <- system.file("extdata", "caop_simplified.gpkg", package = "geopt")
sf::st_layers(gpkg)
sf::st_read(gpkg, layer = "municipio")

The health maps are dissolved from the same simplified freguesias using the pt_health_codes mappings, so their edges align with every administrative level. Each reflects a single health vintage and exists on the current freguesia map only. pt_uls, pt_reg_saude, and pt_aces are freguesia-accurate: units that split municipalities are drawn correctly.

pt_uls has 55 units: 39 mainland ULS plus the island health units, which are not ULS — the Açores have nine Unidades de Saúde de Ilha ("USI São Miguel", ...) and Madeira seven centros de saúde ("CS Funchal Zona I", ...). pt_reg_saude carries the seven regiões de saúde. Both are the 2024 reform.

pt_aces has 71 Agrupamentos de Centros de Saúde — the organization the 2024 reform superseded. Its reg_saude is the region of that time (the former ARS), not the 2024 região de saúde.

pt_uls_municipio (50 units) and pt_aces_municipio (66) are for data by municipality, which can't be divided between the units that share a municipality. Those units are merged into one, named after its members ("ULS Santo António + São João"), so every unit is a set of whole municipalities. Lomba, the one freguesia of Gondomar in ULS Vila Nova de Gaia/Espinho and ACES Espinho/Gaia, is drawn with the rest of Gondomar, where data by municipality counts it. They hold the units of the uls_municipio and aces_municipio columns that pt_join() adds.

All datasets carry nuts1_cod and nuts1, so a health map can be filtered to the mainland, the Açores ("PT2") or Madeira ("PT3"), and pt_aces and pt_aces_municipio carry their reg_saude. They carry no other region column, because no other is the same throughout every unit: ULS Médio Tejo, for example, is split between two regiões de saúde.

See also

pt_lookup() for the geometry-free lookup table, get_map() for composed maps with island insets.
